# Functional Parity Catalog

<!-- GENERATED FILE — do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Regenerate with: python3 tests/functional/generate_catalog.py (inside the test image). -->

Every case below is a complete JSON request that is POSTed to the running Quantra server and whose response is asserted to match an independent QuantLib reference (`tests/contract/ql_reference.py`). Pricing cases compare the returned NPV within a tolerance of 0.01; curve- and vol-surface-sampling cases compare every point of every returned series element-wise within 1e-9; calendar date-utility cases must match the reference dates exactly (no tolerance); calibration cases compare every calibrated parameter / fit statistic within 1e-7. The cases, groupings and descriptions all come from one place — `tests/functional/manifest.py` — and the assertions run inside the standard gate (`bash tests/run_all_tests.sh`, suite 3). See `tests/functional/README.md` for how to add a case.

| **SABR per-node calibration, 3-strike exact fit**<br><sub>Per-node SABR calibration of a 2x2 (1Y/2Y into 5Y/10Y) smile cube quoted at three strike spreads (-100/0/+100bp) with beta fixed at 0.5: three free parameters against three points, so every node fits exactly (per-node RMSE 0) at interior parameters. Compares the per-node forwards, the calibrated alpha/beta/rho/nu grids, the Hagan ATM vols and the fit RMSEs.</sub> | `SABR calibrate`, `beta fixed 0.5`, `exact fit`, `per-node forwards`, `alpha/rho/nu grids` | [sabrcal_eur_2x2_beta_fixed_exact_fit.json](../../examples/data/vol/sabrcal_eur_2x2_beta_fixed_exact_fit.json) | overall_rmse=7.11972e-16, 4-point grids x7 |
| **SABR round-trip: 5-strike smiles from known parameters**<br><sub>The same 2x2 cube quoted at five strike spreads whose vols were generated from known interior SABR parameters (alpha 0.040-0.046, rho -0.25 to -0.18, nu 0.30-0.35, beta 0.5) at the curve's own forwards: the per-node fits are overdetermined (5 points, 3 free parameters) yet recover the generating parameters, leaving only the 1e-8 vol-rounding residual. Pins the calibrator against a known answer.</sub> | `SABR calibrate`, `parameter round-trip`, `overdetermined fit`, `5 strike spreads`, `interior parameters` | [sabrcal_eur_2x2_5strike_roundtrip.json](../../examples/data/vol/sabrcal_eur_2x2_5strike_roundtrip.json) | overall_rmse=1.72766e-09, 4-point grids x7 |
| **SABR round-trip with vega-weighted smile fit**<br><sub>The 5-strike round-trip cube refit with vega_weighted_smile_fit=true, so the per-node objective weights residuals by Black vega instead of equally. On SABR-consistent data the fit still recovers the generating parameters (to ~1e-7), pinning the vega-weighting flag through the calibrator on both sides.</sub> | `SABR calibrate`, `vega-weighted fit`, `parameter round-trip`, `5 strike spreads` | [sabrcal_eur_2x2_5strike_vega_weighted.json](../../examples/data/vol/sabrcal_eur_2x2_5strike_vega_weighted.json) | overall_rmse=1.68127e-09, 4-point grids x7 |

## Correlation / Calibration

| Case | What it exercises | Request JSON | QuantLib value |

| **NDX / RTY correlation from one year of daily closes, no shrinkage**<br><sub>Historical correlation of the Nasdaq-100 and the Russell 2000 from 253 daily closes (2025-09-29 to 2026-09-30, index closes from Yahoo Finance history pages): inner join on dates, daily log returns, sample correlation (the 0.747 the Scotia structured-note example is booked with), no shrinkage, eigenvalue floor not needed. Compares the returned CorrelationMatrixSpec values, the sample correlation, the shrinkage target and intensity, the smallest eigenvalues, the observation counts and the Act/252 realised volatilities.</sub> | `historical correlation`, `log returns`, `date alignment`, `realised volatility`, `correlation spec` | [ndx_rut_closes_2025-09-29_to_2026-09-30.json](../../examples/data/correlation/ndx_rut_closes_2025-09-29_to_2026-09-30.json) | n_rows=2, n_cols=2, shrinkage_target=0.747207, shrinkage_intensity_used=0, eigenvalue_floor_applied=0, smallest_eigenvalue_before=0.252793, smallest_eigenvalue_after=0.252793, observations_used=253, returns_used=252, observations=253, dropped=0, annualised_volatility=0.199096, observations=253, dropped=0, annualised_volatility=0.186663, min_overlap=60, eigenvalue_floor=1e-08, 4-point grids x2 |
| **NDX / RTY / SPX correlation with Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage**<br><sub>Three index series (Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000, S&P 500) over a 365-calendar-day window back from 2026-10-19 (251 common closes), daily log returns, Ledoit-Wolf (2004) shrinkage toward the constant-correlation target. Compares the shrunk matrix, the unshrunk sample correlation, the target and the intensity, the eigenvalue report, the counts (closes outside the window dropped per series) and the realised volatilities.</sub> | `historical correlation`, `Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage`, `constant-correlation target`, `window`, `correlation spec` | [ndx_rty_spx_closes_2025-10-17_to_2026-10-19.json](../../examples/data/correlation/ndx_rty_spx_closes_2025-10-17_to_2026-10-19.json) | n_rows=3, n_cols=3, shrinkage_target=0.833004, shrinkage_intensity_used=0.225732, eigenvalue_floor_applied=0, smallest_eigenvalue_before=0.0862708, smallest_eigenvalue_after=0.0862708, observations_used=251, returns_used=250, observations=266, dropped=15, annualised_volatility=0.19842, observations=266, dropped=15, annualised_volatility=0.182136, observations=252, dropped=1, annualised_volatility=0.12711, min_overlap=60, eigenvalue_floor=1e-08, 9-point grids x2 |

## Zero Coupon Swaps

| Case | What it exercises | Request JSON | QuantLib value |
|---|---|---|---:|
| **EUR 5Y zero-coupon swap, payer, fixed-payment form**<br><sub>Zero-coupon swap paying a single known fixed cashflow of 170,000 at maturity against one compounded Euribor 6M cashflow on 1m base nominal (TARGET, Modified Following, 2025-01-17 to 2030-01-17). The fixed payment sits above the swap's fair payment, so the payer of fixed is underwater. Discounted and projected on the single EUR deposit+swap curve.</sub> | `zero-coupon swap`, `payer`, `fixed-payment form`, `Euribor6M compounded`, `single curve` | [zcs_eur_payer_fixed_payment.json](../../examples/data/zero_coupon_swap/zcs_eur_payer_fixed_payment.json) | -4,206.12 |
| **EUR 5Y zero-coupon swap, receiver, fixed-rate form**<br><sub>The receiver side quoted in the fixed-rate form: a 3.20% fixed rate compounded over the 5Y life under a 30/360 day count (N^FIX = N[(1+R)^alpha - 1]) against one compounded Euribor 6M cashflow on 1m base nominal. The implied fixed payment is above the fair payment, so the receiver of fixed is ahead. Exercises the fixed-rate constructor and its day-count-driven compounding.</sub> | `zero-coupon swap`, `receiver`, `fixed-rate form`, `30/360 compounding`, `sign flip` | [zcs_eur_receiver_fixed_rate.json](../../examples/data/zero_coupon_swap/zcs_eur_receiver_fixed_rate.json) | 4,697.81 |
| **EUR 5Y zero-coupon swap, payer at the fair payment**<br><sub>The same payer trade struck at the swap's fair fixed payment (165,098.6955), so both legs have equal present value and the NPV is zero. Pins the fair-payment solve end to end: the fixed payment that makes the contract par reproduces a ~0 NPV on both the server and the QuantLib reference.</sub> | `zero-coupon swap`, `payer`, `fair fixed payment`, `par NPV`, `fixed-payment form` | [zcs_eur_payer_at_fair_payment.json](../../examples/data/zero_coupon_swap/zcs_eur_payer_at_fair_payment.json) | 0.00 |

## Callable Bonds

| Case | What it exercises | Request JSON | QuantLib value |
|---|---|---|---:|
| **EUR 8Y 5% callable bond, single call at 100 (deep in the money)**<br><sub>High-coupon (5% annual 30/360) 8Y EUR bond on a ~3% curve, so the straight bond trades well above par (NPV 1,127,246.83). A single issuer call at a clean 100 in 2029 is deep in the issuer's favour, so the Hull-White tree (a=0.03, sigma=0.01, 500 steps) prices the callable at 1,065,161.03 — 62,085.81 below the straight bond, the value of the embedded call.</sub> | `callable bond`, `in-the-money call`, `Hull-White tree`, `callable below straight`, `explicit HW params` | [cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_call_100_itm.json](../../examples/data/callable_bonds/cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_call_100_itm.json) | 1,065,161.03 |
| **EUR 8Y 5% callable bond, single call at 115 (out of the money)**<br><sub>The same 5% premium bond, but the single 2029 call is struck at a clean 115 — above the bond's premium price, so the call almost never bites. The callable prices at 1,123,370.51, only 3,876.33 below the straight bond (1,127,246.83): an out-of-the-money call leaves the bond close to the plain fixed-rate value.</sub> | `callable bond`, `out-of-the-money call`, `callable near straight`, `Hull-White tree` | [cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_call_115_otm.json](../../examples/data/callable_bonds/cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_call_115_otm.json) | 1,123,370.51 |
| **EUR 8Y 5% callable bond, 3-date step-down call schedule**<br><sub>The 5% premium bond with a three-date American-style call ladder (2029 at 102, 2030 at 101, 2031 at 100.5). The multi-date callability lets the issuer redeem at the most favourable of the stepping prices, pricing the callable at 1,076,386.15 — 50,860.68 below the straight bond. Exercises a multi-entry CallabilitySchedule.</sub> | `callable bond`, `multi-date call schedule`, `step-down call prices`, `Hull-White tree` | [cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_multi_call_step.json](../../examples/data/callable_bonds/cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_multi_call_step.json) | 1,076,386.15 |
| **EUR 8Y 2% puttable bond, single put at 98**<br><sub>Low-coupon (2% annual 30/360) 8Y EUR bond on the same ~3% curve, so the straight bond trades at a discount (NPV 917,757.88). A single bondholder put at a clean 98 in 2029 lets the holder sell the bond back above its market value, raising the puttable price to 955,355.35 — 37,597.47 ABOVE the straight bond, the value of the embedded put.</sub> | `puttable bond`, `in-the-money put`, `puttable above straight`, `Hull-White tree` | [cfrb_eur_8y_2pct_put_98.json](../../examples/data/callable_bonds/cfrb_eur_8y_2pct_put_98.json) | 955,355.35 |
